extracted.intended_audience: improv performers/teams, showrunners, and festival-goers interested in Del Close Marathon submissions and event details
extracted.subtask_short: festival submission for Del Close Marathon
extracted.subtask_description: Information and requirements for applying to perform at the Del Close Marathon (DCM22), plus high-level programming/format details and logistics for the 2026 edition. Useful for performers, teams, and organizers planning submissions or attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event dates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival runs on these specific dates; performers must be available for June 12–14, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition identifier
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This listing pertains to the 22nd edition (DCM22) of the Del Close Marathon; edition-specific rules, programming, and contacts apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performances will take place in New York City; applicants should be able to perform at NYC venues or coordinate travel/logistics accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming is in English; submissions/performances should be suitable for English-language presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizing body
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival is produced by UCB; organizational standards, venue choices, and curation are managed by UCB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival format / duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The format features roughly 56 hours of continuous improv across multiple stages and venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect back-to-back, marathon-style scheduling across venues; formats that fit continuous/multi-stage programming are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming scope (eligible genres)
rubrics_metrics.description: This edition expands beyond pure improv for the first time, welcoming stand-up, podcasts, sketch comedy, and alternative programming alongside the traditional improv lineup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are not limited to improv teams; non-improv formats (stand-up, podcasts, sketch, alternative) are explicitly welcomed for DCM22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission window
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions for DCM22 opened February 2 and closed February 28, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications outside this window were not accepted for DCM22; future editions will have their own fixed submission periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories included improv teams, improv show formats, late-night bit show pitches, and non-improv/alternative programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit to one of the listed categories; prepare materials specific to the chosen category (team packet, show format description, bit show pitch, or alternative programming proposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission fee and fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission fee was $15 ($5 for late-night bit shows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different categories had different fees; applicants should note the fee for their category and be prepared to pay at submission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waivers availability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers could be requested (or were offered) to reduce or eliminate the submission fee—applicants needing financial accommodation could apply for a waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct outreach to specific teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Harold teams on both coasts were contacted directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers proactively invited existing Harold teams, suggesting targeted outreach and possible preferential or direct-selection consideration for established Harold ensembles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-marathon headliner showcases / venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-marathon headliner showcases take place at Theater for the New City and UCBNY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headliner-related showcases were scheduled at specific venues ahead of the marathon; applicants/attendees should be aware of related events hosted at partner venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headliner lineup (programming signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headliners include established acts such as Bigger! w/ Brennan Lee Mulligan and Izzy Roland, Rory Scovel, Yeti, Improv4humans with Matt Besser, The Big Team, Big Grande, Dinosaur w/ Paul Scheer, Astronomy Club, Adam Conover & Friends, the 10th Anniversary of Asian AF, and several all-star ASSSSCAT ensembles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The high-profile headliner roster indicates the festival’s prestige and the type/level of acts programmed; applicants can gauge fit and expected audience by reviewing the headliner slate.
